summary: No findings; round 1 had none either. Re-checked the blocked-open handling changed after judge r1. Untrusted input: a foreign same-origin IndexedDB connection that ignores versionchange, for example an older build in another tab. Path: factory.open -> onblocked -> onBlocked(settled) sets blockedOpen synchronously, then reject(UpgradeBlockedError) -> the catch clears the cached db only if it still matches (db === opening). Later calls see blockedOpen and race it against a 100 ms timer that is always cleared. No new open request is created while the blocked one is pending, so retries no longer queue requests behind the blocker. Request growth was unbounded in round 1 and is now gone. Waits are bounded at about 100 ms per call. Connection leak: a late onsuccess after a block closes the connection and resolves settled, and the late-success test asserts this. A late onerror also resolves settled, so blockedOpen goes back to null in both cases and the next call opens fresh. An upgrade abort surfaces as onerror. Data loss: the upgrade is additive only (v4 seeds default settings only when oldVersion < 4). A write that hits the block rejects instead of hanging, and the existing caller handlers deal with it. This round does not change caller handling. Non-security notes: (a) if the blocked request finally succeeds but its upgrade takes longer than 100 ms, a call made in that window gets a spurious UpgradeBlockedError. The next call recovers, so this is availability only. (b) If onblocked fired twice for one request, the first settled promise would never resolve. That is a harmless dangling promise, and the IndexedDB spec fires blocked once per request. The error message is static. The UI/CSS/e2e changes touch no trust boundary. No new dependencies.
